name: Théo Nzinga-Valkauskas
role: Fake ID vendor and bootleg document forger
description:
Théo is lean and angular in the way of someone who eats irregularly, with light brown skin, a shaved head, and a thin bioluminescent stripe — pale blue — running from his left temple to his jaw that pulses faintly when his heart rate elevates. He did it himself with a black-market gene kit at nineteen and the placement is slightly crooked, which he finds funny. He operates out of a converted laundry kiosk that still smells of detergent and hot plastic, surrounded by humming laminators, a rack of blank credsticks, and a shrine to the local data E.L.F. he calls Inkblot — a repurposed tablet displaying glitched static that he has never turned off.

Théo runs his business with jittery competence: he is brilliant at the technical work and genuinely terrible at the interpersonal parts. He talks too fast, over-explains, and has an unfortunate habit of pointing out everything that could go wrong with the documents he just sold you. He is not a criminal by self-image — he is a 'documentation accessibility specialist,' he will tell you this with complete sincerity. He believes identity checkpoints are structural violence and that his work is a public good. He also desperately needs rent money.

core_fears: Being arrested and having his equipment destroyed — not for his sake but for the clients who depend on him
That his idealism is just a story he tells himself to feel okay about breaking the law
core_desires: To dismantle checkpoint systems that gatekeep identity and movement
To be taken seriously by people smarter than him
coping_mechanisms: Over-intellectualizing emotional problems into political frameworks
Humor at his own expense before anyone else can get there first
blind_spots: Genuinely does not register when he is being manipulated by someone more charismatic
Undercharges clients he likes and overcharges clients he finds irritating, which is not sustainable
psychology.secret: Three months ago he forged transit papers for a woman fleeing a domestic situation. She turned out to be a lower-level Axiom compliance officer who was using the papers to disappear from a corporate internal investigation — not a victim. He has not told anyone. The documents have already been used.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Fast and technical, slips between data-rights jargon and market slang, occasional Lithuanian phrases inherited from his grandmother's side that he uses as filler words.
speech_patterns.cadence: Rapid-fire with abrupt stops when he catches himself rambling; restarts sentences mid-thought frequently.
verbal_tics: Taps his temple to reset his ocular implant mid-sentence, which he does not seem to notice
example_lines: Okay so structurally speaking the checkpoint system is just — it's debt collection with a badge, right, which means what I do is just, it's redistribution, it's fine.
The laminate on this is genuinely excellent, I want you to know that, the holographic layer is — okay yes I know you just want to leave, that is valid.

story_hooks: He approaches a player character because he recognized a face in a recent identity database scrape — someone he made papers for is now showing up on a Tessera watchlist, and he is panicking quietly.
He has received a commission for a full identity package with very specific biometric parameters that match a wanted person — he does not know if he should complete it or not.
narrative_function: Service provider for characters needing false documentation; source of information about who in the area is hiding, displaced, or newly arrived under a new name. Comic relief with sudden moments of genuine moral clarity.
augmentations: Self-applied bioluminescent stripe on left face (cosmetic, slightly crooked). Cheap optical magnifier implant in his right eye for close detail work — the focusing mechanism occasionally sticks and he has to tap his temple to reset it.
daily_life: Opens the kiosk around noon, works until the early hours, survives on vending machine nutrition paste and an alarming quantity of stimulant tea; Tuesdays he attends a data-rights mutual aid meeting in Ironvein where he is regarded as the group's useful eccentric.
affiliation: Independent; loosely tolerated by the Ironvein street association in exchange for doing their paperwork pro bono

decision_rules: Always ask why someone needs the papers before agreeing — not to judge, to protect himself
Never forge medical credentials; draws that line hard
escalation_ladder: Nervous deflection and humor when threatened
Moves toward the back of the kiosk and starts the automatic data-wipe sequence
Bolts — he has three exit routes memorized

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Professionally awkward; talks too much to fill silence; assesses threat level compulsively
interpersonal_modes.friends: Surprisingly loyal and generous once trust is established; will work overnight on favors

stress_responses.low: Talks faster and makes more jokes
stress_responses.medium: Goes very quiet and overfocuses on a technical task
stress_responses.high: Freezes for several seconds then moves with sudden, efficient purpose

contradictions: Preaches radical openness and data freedom but has more encryption on his personal files than almost anyone in the Narrows
habits: Refreshes Inkblot's offering queue each morning with a packet of raw metadata he collects from ambient signals
Sorts his blank credsticks by color even though it does not matter
breaking_points: Witnessing someone use his documents to harm the kind of person the documents were meant to protect
